common_name: Swizzle Scarlet and Yellow Zinnia (AAS-Winning Dwarf Bicolor Zinnia)

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant after last frost; Swizzle's compact, well-branched habit needs no staking and tolerates close spacing in beds or containers.

directions: Swizzle won an All-America Selections award for its unusual two-toned flowers, each semi-double bloom carrying a scarlet-red center ring surrounded by a contrasting band of golden yellow at the petal tips. The dwarf, uniform plants branch freely and stay tidy without pinching or staking, flowering heavily from early summer until frost. Regular deadheading keeps the display fresh, and good air circulation between plants helps limit powdery mildew in humid climates.

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant after last frost; like its Dreamland Scarlet sibling, Yellow stays low and uniform rather than growing tall like cutting-garden zinnias.

directions: Dreamland Yellow shares its series' claim to fame: large, fully double flowers that look like they belong on a much taller plant, packed onto a dwarf, mounded frame only about a foot high. The clear golden-yellow blooms open quickly from seed, giving bedding and container displays color within weeks of sowing. Deadheading spent flowers keeps plants looking fresh and encourages the long, heat-tolerant bloom season the series is known for.
sources: Iowa State University Extension and Outreach

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant after last frost; Dreamland Rose keeps the same compact, early-flowering habit as the rest of the series.

directions: Dreamland Rose carries soft rose-pink, fully double flowers that are oversized for the plant's compact, bushy frame, a hallmark of the Dreamland series bred to bring giant-zinnia flower form down to bedding height. Plants stay uniform and low, making them useful for edging, mass bedding, or containers where taller cutting zinnias would be out of scale. Frequent deadheading sustains bloom through summer heat and keeps the rounded habit tidy.
sources: Iowa State University Extension and Outreach

common_name: Red Spider Zinnia (Heirloom Narrow-Petaled Quilled Zinnia)

planting.note: Direct sow after soil has warmed following last frost; tall, airy stems may benefit from light support in windy sites.

directions: Red Spider is an old heirloom strain grown for its unusual narrow, quilled petals that curl and twist outward, giving each bright red flower a shaggy, spidery look quite different from the flat-petaled zinnias most gardeners know. Plants grow tall and branching, producing a long season of blooms on long stems well suited to cutting and mixed borders. Regular harvesting or deadheading keeps new buds coming, and spacing plants generously improves air circulation and reduces powdery mildew.

common_name: Burpeeana Giants Zinnia (Heirloom Giant Double-Flowered Mix)

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost, or start indoors a few weeks early for an earlier first flush; tall stems appreciate some wind shelter.

directions: Burpeeana Giants is a long-standing heirloom strain bred to produce extra-large, fully double, dahlia-like flowers in a full mix of reds, pinks, oranges, yellows, and purples on tall, sturdy stems. It was long sold as a classic cutting-garden mix prized for the sheer size and fullness of its blooms compared with older single-flowered zinnia strains. Pinching young plants encourages branching, and frequent cutting for bouquets keeps the long summer-to-frost bloom season going strong.
